quizName: Hardest Questions in Minnesota Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to easily reach and use all the controls.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the most important action you can take to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: When it is obvious that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need to use a turn signal at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use turn signals every time you turn or change lanes. Use them even if you think your intentions are obvious or no one else is around. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: Which of the following does not protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye or face protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, ankle-covering boots or shoes, and durable gloves.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles provide the best protection. Laced boots are best. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: Penalties for riding while impaired may include:
questions.explanation: If convicted of riding while impaired, you may face fines, license suspension, jail time, court costs, legal fees, higher insurance rates, and community service. If you have been drinking, do not ride.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear while riding.
Should not be worn while riding.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, preferably leather, for protection. In warm weather, leather jackets help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend in with traffic and not be noticed.
Not use turn signals unless you are riding at night.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride closely behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use turn signals, your brake light, and proper lane position to communicate. Keep enough distance from other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are not very important because motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.
Are very important to alert other drivers to your plans.
Should not be used if no vehicles are close to you.
Are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to alert other drivers to your plans.
questions.explanation: As a motorcyclist, you are more vulnerable, so use turn signals to alert others to your plans. Always use them when you change lanes or turn, even if no one seems to be nearby.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces provide poor traction for tires. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal plates are more hazardous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: Some surfaces are slippery and hard to control on a motorcycle. Which surface is slippery?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road are all slippery. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly watch the road ahead for:
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for changing traffic, hazardous road conditions, and possible escape routes. Stay ready to react to any changes.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast can:

options.text: Cause the rider to go into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Often keeps the rider in their lane.
Is safe because motorcycles are smaller.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause the rider to go into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire that is not fully inflated may still look fine, so you cannot rely on your eyes alone.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. You should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder, away from traffic.

questions.explanation: Most crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright-colored clothing at all times to be more visible to other drivers, even during the day.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Limits your movement to one area of the lane.
Lets you rely on others to spot hazards.
Requires you to ride faster with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make hands too hot.
Be worn to grip the handgrips better.
Not be worn because they make controls harder to use.
Be worn only on cold days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to grip the handgrips better.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They give you a better grip on the handgrips and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have which types of brakes?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may pull out into your path without looking.
Others may drive slowly while looking for spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out into your path without looking.
questions.explanation: A driver may unexpectedly pull out of a parking spot into your path. Car doors may open into your lane, and pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: For the best protection, use a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no visible defects.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riding requires a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up.
Get off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, take rest breaks every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you cannot do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Riding gloves are usually:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head and neck injuries in a crash. It does not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothing should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely, but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever makes you most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: For adequate protection while riding, wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: For your safety, know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine.

questions.question: When using an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good riding condition.
Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride as you usually do, since most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn the gear pattern first.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads instead.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Stop them any way you can, including taking their keys. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: Which fabric gives motorcyclists the most protection?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection when riding.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet for the best protection, you should pick one that:

options.text: Has been in a crash before.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the best protection. The helmet should fit snugly around your head.

questions.question: Which item does NOT need regular checking?
questions.explanation: Check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes before every ride. Small mechanical problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: Where is the best source of information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who owns a different motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding any motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are borrowing a motorcycle.

questions.question: For the best protection, boots or shoes should:

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover the ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Keep heels low so they don't catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they don't get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: What can remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce alcohol's effects. They may help you stay awake, but they cannot make you sober.

questions.question: Which color helps you be seen while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible while riding. Wear bright clothing any time of day.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing that includes sturdy jackets and pants covering your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.
